pigments.label: Chlorophyll
pigments.note: Two bands BRACKETING the green. Leaves are green because chlorophyll reflects the band the Sun is strongest in rather than absorbing it — the single fact every reader brings to this page, and the one a naive energy-maximiser gets wrong.

pigments.label: Bacteriorhodopsin
pigments.note: A retinal pigment absorbing straight through the green-yellow, so it presents purple. The purple-Earth hypothesis argues organisms like this took that band first and left chlorophyll what remained.

pigments.label: Carotenes
pigments.note: Blue absorbers reflecting orange. On Earth they are accessory pigments doing photoprotection as much as capture.

pigments.label: Phycoerythrin
pigments.note: Harvests the blue-green that penetrates deep water; presents pink-red.

pigments.label: Phycocyanin
pigments.note: An orange-red absorber presenting blue-cyan — the pigment favoured where a star throws its light short of the red.

pigments.label: Pheophytin
pigments.note: Chlorophyll with the magnesium gone: the same bracketing shape, shifted and weaker, presenting olive-brown.

pigments.label: Melanin
pigments.note: Broadband absorption rising into the ultraviolet. It works under any star, which is why it must never be selected OUT by a threshold — it presents black, and under a starved sky it wins.
